notes: The argument branches after extrusion into a mechanical line (grain refinement + MgZn2/ND dispersion -> attributed Hall-Petch/Orowan/CTE-mismatch strengthening -> yield peak near 0.1 wt%) and a thermal line (ND/matrix interfaces -> argued interface constraint -> 72% lower CTE -> dimensional stability); thermal conductivity is a side branch that only re-enters at the 0.05 wt% design guidance. Figures show three things the text misreads: compression yield peaks at 0.15 wt% (F8b); residual strain is not monotone in ND (F9b); the 72% CTE step at ~0.03 vol% ND (F9c-d) exceeds any mixture bound, so the thermal branch rests on an argued mechanism with a likely alloy/composite offset. Lost: Table 1 (not in packet), the Cp and phonon Umklapp argument behind the 473 K conductivity maxima, texture differences visible in XRD intensity ratios, and scale-label errors (F2b, F7c 10x; F10b axis). Judge: the F7c interlayer is at MgZn2/alpha-Mg in both figure and text; the ND attribution is a MatMech-summary error, so it is recorded on o7c, not as an audit.

changes: Overturned audit o7c: removed o7c -qualifies-> c18 and text_silent; the ~8 nm interlayer is at MgZn2/alpha-Mg in both F7c and the paper text, the ND attribution came only from the MatMech summary (ruling #37). o7c now evidences s_int2 only; c18 note and case notes rewritten.

o28 provenance measured -> derived; added o9cd -derives-> o28 (convert_to_quantity, via=known_relation, relative change); image_note softened: offset between alloy and composites is possible, untested, and the figure agrees with the text numbers.
o8b image_note: the 0.15 wt% compression curve has a yield-point drop, so its lead over 0.1 wt% holds for peak and 0.2%-offset readings (the figure contradicts the text's ranking).
key_multimodal_steps: Register colocated views (F6): the HAADF bright particle, the Zn/Mg EDX maps and the 365 nm line scan are overlaid to name the particle MgZn2, converging with the XRD assignment (F3) that the figure only marks on one trace.

Correlate across series (F4f x F8a -> o24): grain size and yield across the ND series do not co-vary (0.05 wt% stronger at unchanged grain size, finest 0.2 wt% weaker), so the attributed Hall-Petch lead term is qualified.

Convert strain to CTE and compare with the text (F9a-d, F10): per-heating strain / 273 K reproduces 3.08e-5 and 8.6e-6 /K, but the cycle-5 residual strain in F9b is highest at 0.1 wt%, against the text's 'stability improves with ND content'.
review.audit_summary: Confirmed 4: o8b and o_res (figure contradicts the text: compression peak at 0.15 wt%; residual strain not monotone), o24 (figure-derived series undercuts attributed Hall-Petch), o28 (figure agrees with the numbers, but a 72% step at ~0.03 vol% is not what the argued interface mechanism predicts). Overturned 1: o7c conflicted with the MatMech summary, not with the paper.
